observation: Museum map titled Sri Lanka — Anuradhapura Period. Visible legend distinguishes canals, sub-capitals, monastery sites and ancient ports over rivers/topography. The map distributes political/religious sites mainly through the dry-zone lowlands and shows coastal gateways around the island.
interpretation: Useful visual model of a coupled inland hydraulic/monastic/political network connected to maritime gateways; not evidence that all mapped sites were simultaneous or equally important.
epistemic_limit: Modern museum cartography; independent archaeological sourcing required for historical claims.

observation: Museum panel titled TRADE / Ancient Sea Routes. Solid curves mark Major Sea Routes; dashed line marks Dhow Technology Zone; x-marked line marks Outrigger Technology Zone. Sri Lanka is placed near the route junction between western Indian Ocean, India, Bay of Bengal and Southeast Asia.
interpretation: Strong as a dezoom illustration of Sri Lanka's geographic position within Indian Ocean circuits. Technology-zone lines are schematic and chronologically underspecified.
epistemic_limit: Do not promote precise dhow/outrigger boundaries, chronology or exclusivity without specialist maritime-archaeology sources.
